position: HYBRID with channel safety: open direct-to-client signup alongside the studio channel, but fork the commercial layer — not the product — so price, attribution, and lead flow all point couples and studios back toward each other rather than around each other.
thesis: The codebase has already built 96% of a second door and then bolted it shut. A couple-owned catalogue (N-73) runs through the exact same wizard, customizer, upload, and publish routes a studio uses — map-client.md confirms only one route in the entire admin API is partner-only (issuing a couple's own sign-in) — yet the only way to get a couple account at all is for a studio to create one first (map-client.md §7 item 1: 'a couple with no wedding and no studio has no way into the product at all'). That gate does not protect studios from competition; it protects nobody, because the couples it excludes are overwhelmingly the ones whose studio was never going to give them Mehfilbox anyway — the ones still on Google Drive, the actual incumbent COMPETITORS.md §1 names. Opening the door does not have to mean opening it around studios. If a direct signup captures which studio shot the wedding — one field — that fact can be turned into a locked attribution credit, a routed lead, and a price the studio's own clients never have to pay, converting the feared 'the platform is stealing my clients' into the true story: the platform is finding studios clients they never had a relationship with in the first place. 'Hybrid pleases nobody' is the right worry about a hybrid that gives both channels the same terms. This one does not — wholesale stays wholesale, free stays free for studios, and every direct-channel rupee is priced and routed to make the studio door look better by comparison, not worse.

moves.name: Capture 'which studio shot this?' at the front door
moves.why: The whole channel-safety model hangs on one fact captured at signup, not discovered later — reuses the couple-shaped step already built for N-73 (components/admin/CreateWizard.tsx:290-337,697-725), so this is a new field on an existing flow, not a new flow.
moves.cost: Small: one wizard step, one FK column on catalogues; no new subsystem.
moves.risk: Couples skip or misreport the studio to reach the cheaper/freer tier — a UX and incentive problem, not a technical one (see risks).

moves.name: Lock attribution before a single direct signup ships, not after
moves.why: map-client.md and map-themes-customizer.md both confirm 'Presented by' and the platform-credit toggle are plain, autosaved ThemePicker fields (components/admin/ThemePicker.tsx:180-315) that any catalogue owner can edit today, including a couple after handover — the four panels hidden from a couple owner (map-client.md §3, app/admin/c/[id]/page.tsx:74-76,206-243) do not include branding. 'Attribution that survives' is currently false in code; it has to become true before it is promised to a studio.
moves.cost: Medium: one new invariant in the branding write path (app/api/admin/catalogues/[id]/route.ts:32-39) — read-only presentedBy/platform-credit whenever origin_org_id names a partner.
moves.risk: None in building it; the only risk is sequencing it after launch instead of before.

moves.name: Route the named lead to the studio, not just display its name
moves.why: PRICING.md's own plan already promises a studio a referral link 'permanently, through every renewal' (PRICING.md:139-142) — not evidenced as built in any of the three subsystem maps read for this brief. The cheapest real version reuses the existing notifications queue, dedupe key, and template pattern already proven live for credit-request/expiry/grace mail (lib/notify/schedule.ts).
moves.cost: Small-to-medium: one new template, one new trigger point; the queue, cron drain, and dedupe pattern already exist.
moves.risk: A named studio with no live Mehfilbox account has nowhere for the lead to land except SUPPORT_EMAIL — the same silent-fallback gap map-client.md §7 item 3 already documents for credit requests — needs an explicit unclaimed-lead list, not a mailto and a shrug.

moves.name: Set the price floor off numbers PRICING.md already publishes
moves.why: Wholesale (₹1,999) was priced for a reseller doing volume; PRICING.md's own suggested retail (₹5,000-8,000) is what a studio is told to charge the same couple. Anchoring a direct/individual Deliver credit in between — recommend testing around ₹3,499 — protects the gap studios rely on without inventing a number from nothing.
moves.cost: Requires credits/plans to carry a channel or price field, which neither has today (map-commerce.md §7 item 3 — plans has zero rows and no reader) — a schema and entitlement addition, not new infrastructure.
moves.risk: ₹3,499 sits above viddrop's real ₹1,900-2,400 band (COMPETITORS.md §2) — deliberately, per the doc's own 'never compete on price per wedding' doctrine (§6) — but it means the direct door loses every pure price comparison and must sell retention and quality instead.

moves.name: Make the theme store the first real use of the entitlement seam that already exists
moves.why: lib/entitlements.ts already resolves catalogue-over-org-over-default, and its own code comment already argues for a couple needing an independent grant once a studio relationship has ended. map-commerce.md §7 item 4 confirms nothing has ever written that catalogue-scoped row. A purchased theme is exactly that: the first real write to a seam the architecture already anticipated.
moves.cost: Medium: the themes table needs an owner/tier/price column (absent from supabase/migrations/0019_themes.sql today), plus one entitlement check added to resolveTheme/themeFrom.
moves.risk: Real engineering competing against the N-77-N-88 backlog and against Razorpay for the same scarce founder-plus-agent time — sequence alongside the core roadmap, not ahead of it.

moves.name: Launch on the manual, invoice-then-grant motion the whole product already runs on
moves.why: map-commerce.md §1 is explicit: every rupee that has moved through this product so far is a platform admin typing a free-text reason into an audit row after money changed hands elsewhere — Razorpay is entirely absent. Hybrid needs a front door, not a checkout, to start; a couple can pay by UPI or transfer and be manually granted a credit or theme unlock exactly as a studio is today.
moves.cost: Near zero beyond move one — a scope decision, not a build.
moves.risk: Doesn't scale past a handful of direct signups without consuming founder time the backlog also needs — the honest argument for prioritizing Razorpay sooner if direct volume proves real, not a reason to wait for it before opening the door.

studio_safety: Attribution becomes a locked field, not an editable one, the instant a catalogue's origin names a partner studio — closing the present gap where any owner, including a couple after handover, can blank 'Presented by' through the customizer (components/admin/ThemePicker.tsx:180-315; app/api/admin/catalogues/[id]/route.ts:32-39).

Every direct signup that names a studio fires a routed lead to that studio, reusing the notifications queue and dedupe pattern already proven for credit-request, expiry and grace mail (lib/notify/schedule.ts) — a couple with no prior Mehfilbox-studio relationship becomes a lead for one, not a bypass of one.

A hard price floor: any product a studio can resell — Deliver credits, Keep/Cinema upgrades, advanced themes — is priced higher direct than wholesale, anchored to PRICING.md's own suggested-retail numbers, so no studio ever sees a client get the same thing cheaper by going around them.

Studio-exclusive surfaces — house styles, team seats, the lapse/renewal worklist, custom domains — stay studio-only at the API layer, not just hidden in the UI, closing the gap map-themes-customizer.md §7 already flags (house-style routes in lib/admin/presets.ts check org_id only, not org kind).

A studio-attributed direct purchase prices advanced themes at or near the studio's own free-access level, or credits the studio directly — a past client's later purchase still pays the studio, not only the platform.

The Studio plan's own arithmetic stays strictly cheaper per wedding than any direct path at real volume: PRICING.md's own line, 'a studio that delivers three weddings has paid nothing for the platform,' remains true and undercuts any direct price by construction, so a volume professional has no rational reason to leave the studio door.

The product experience does not fork — a couple's console is already, today, the identical customizer/publish/upload surface a studio uses (map-client.md §3) — so channel safety lives entirely in price and entitlement rules layered on one shared codebase, cheap enough for a one-founder-plus-agent team to actually build, ship and keep honest.
theme_store_model: Nothing here exists yet — themes are entirely platform-global today: no owner, price, SKU, version, or entitlement check anywhere in the code (themes table, supabase/migrations/0019_themes.sql:9-19, has no tenant column at all; map-themes-customizer.md §7 confirms zero purchase flow, zero third-party author role, zero 'locked until bought' state). This is a build proposal grounded in the seams the architecture already has, not a description of a working feature. Two tiers. FREE stays exactly what it is today: the seven built-ins plus whatever a platform admin authors, available to every studio-plan org and every catalogue that traces its origin to one, studio-run or handed-over/couple-owned alike — nothing changes for a studio, which is the point; it is not a new benefit to build, it is the status quo restated as the differentiator. ADVANCED is a small, deliberately curated set of new platform-authored themes, built the same way today's are at /admin/platform/themes — no marketplace, no third-party submissions, no versioning system is proposed, because none of that exists and building it is a materially larger project than tiering what is already there. The access check: add one clause to resolveTheme/themeFrom (themes/registry.ts:154-160) so an Advanced theme renders when the catalogue's origin org is on an active Studio plan (free, bundled, studios never see a per-theme charge), or the catalogue carries a catalogue-scoped theme entitlement written by a purchase. That second path is not new infrastructure: lib/entitlements.ts already resolves catalogue-over-org-over-default, and its own code comment already argues for exactly this case — a couple with no ongoing studio relationship needing an independent grant — but map-commerce.md §7 item 4 confirms nothing has ever written that catalogue-scoped row. The theme store is the first real use of a seam the product already designed for. Pricing: one-time per catalogue, not a subscription, matching the product's per-wedding shape throughout PRICING.md — anchored below the Extra-4K add-on (₹1,999 per 20 minutes) and roughly in line with a few months of Extra Storage (₹25/GB/month), so recommend testing ₹499-999 per Advanced theme. Does the studio earn? Yes, whenever the purchasing catalogue names an originating studio: the cleanest version needs no revenue-share accounting, no invoice-splitting and no payment integration to exist on day one — a catalogue with a named studio simply prices the Advanced theme at ₹0, funded by attribution value rather than a cash split. 'Name your studio' becomes the actual discount code: free if the studio is on the Studio plan, free-by-referral-credit if not yet, and only a truly unaffiliated direct catalogue ever pays the ₹499-999 individual price. That is the only path that needs real payment rails, and it can be built second, behind or alongside Razorpay (N-20), which the product needs regardless of whether a theme store ships.
pricing_implications: Studio wholesale is untouched: ₹1,999 Deliver, ₹4,999/yr Studio plan with 3 bundled credits, unchanged — this is the relationship the whole plan protects, not renegotiates. One new SKU is needed: a direct/individual Deliver credit, recommended to test around ₹3,499 (excl. GST, consistent with PRICING.md's own convention) — deliberately above viddrop's real ₹1,900-2,400 band (COMPETITORS.md §2) and below PRICING.md's own suggested-retail floor (₹5,000). That positioning follows COMPETITORS.md's own doctrine (§6, §8) — 'never compete on price per wedding,' 'their deletion is our funnel' — applied to a new channel rather than invented for it: the direct door sells retention and quality against viddrop, not a lower number. Theme-store pricing is additive and mostly non-cash: free for any studio-plan-linked catalogue (a retention feature, not a new revenue line, exactly as the founder's own free-themes-for-studios framing intends), ₹0 for any individual who names a studio (the discount is the attribution, not a rev-share), and ₹499-999 one-time only for a genuinely unaffiliated catalogue. None of this has anywhere to live yet: map-commerce.md §7 confirms the plans table is empty and unread, catalogue-level entitlements are never written, and Razorpay is entirely absent — zero code, zero webhooks, zero env vars. So every price above must launch on the same manual, admin-grants-after-a-bank-transfer motion the whole platform already runs on. That is a feature, not a shortcut: hybrid's first version costs a signup form and a pricing decision, not a payments project, and defers the real payments build to exactly when direct volume proves it is needed rather than before it. GST treatment is unchanged — PRICING.md's existing exclusive-with-inclusive-beside-it convention (§6) extends to any new SKU without a new tax decision.
risks: Sequencing risk, the biggest one: attribution is editable by any catalogue owner today, confirmed in both map-client.md and map-themes-customizer.md (ThemePicker.tsx:180-315 exposes 'Presented by' as a plain autosaved field, and the four panels hidden from a couple owner per map-client.md §3 do not include branding). If direct signup ships before that field is locked, the very first direct couples can delete studio credit the day they sign in — the channel-safety promise would be false in code before it is tested in the market.

Zero payment infrastructure exists to carry any of this: Razorpay is entirely unbuilt (map-commerce.md §1, §7 item 1), the plans table has zero rows and no reader, and no route has ever written a catalogue-scoped entitlement. Every price in this plan launches as a manually-granted, admin-typed transaction, which does not scale past a handful of direct signups without consuming founder time the N-77-N-88 backlog also needs.

Pricing-floor complexity is real: carrying two effective prices for the same Deliver credit needs a channel or price field the credits/plans schema does not have today (map-commerce.md §5, §7 item 3), and gets harder to defend the moment a direct customer and a studio's client compare notes.

Signaling risk independent of mechanics: a studio can read any direct door, however safety-railed, as evidence of future intent to go around them — the floor and the lock have to be stated publicly and kept, not just implemented quietly, which is itself a commitment that is harder to walk back if direct volume later turns out to matter more than expected.

The entire free-unlock design leans on 'name your studio' being honest. A couple who omits or misnames a real studio to dodge the individual price is a fraud vector this design has no code-level way to catch, only a UX nudge, not a control.

Direct/individual pricing is deliberately set above viddrop's real per-wedding price (COMPETITORS.md §2, §6) rather than competing on price — correct per the document's own doctrine, but it means the direct door will lose every pure price comparison and caps how much volume it can realistically bring in on its own.

The 'pleases nobody' risk is real, not just rhetorical, even with these mechanisms: a studio may still feel a direct door legitimizes 'can't I just do this myself' even at a worse price, and an individual may resent that a studio's client gets the functionally same product cheaper, bundled inside ₹4,999/yr, than they do standalone. Both frictions are managed by the moves above, not eliminated — only the metrics below, run for real, will show whether the floor and the lock are enough.
metrics: Share of direct signups that name an originating studio — the primary check on whether the channel-safety design is used rather than routed around; a low share is the earliest warning sign of cannibalization rather than addition.

Studio-plan renewal rate and wholesale-credit volume, before vs after the direct door opens — the one number that would actually prove or disprove the studio-side 'pleases nobody' fear; any dip coincident with direct-signup growth is the kill signal.

Lead-to-studio-plan conversion: what share of routed studio-lead notifications, from a direct signup naming them, result in that studio's own account activity — a new Studio-plan signup or a wholesale credit purchase — within 90 days.

Realized direct/individual Deliver price against viddrop's ₹1,900-2,400 band and against PRICING.md's own ₹5,000-8,000 suggested-retail floor (COMPETITORS.md §2, §6) — tracks whether the price floor lands in the intended gap or drifts to an edge.

Theme-store attach rate and revenue split between studio-plan-linked (₹0) and unaffiliated-individual (paid) catalogues — the direct test of whether 'free for studios, paid for individuals' produces real incremental revenue or just build cost with no uptake.

Founder and support time spent per direct signup on manual credit-grant and theme-unlock admin actions — since no self-serve payment exists yet, this is the concrete ceiling on how far hybrid scales before Razorpay becomes mandatory rather than optional.

Count of attribution-lock or lead-routing failures — a catalogue where presentedBy was successfully edited despite a named studio, or a named-studio lead that landed nowhere but the SUPPORT_EMAIL fallback map-client.md §7 item 3 already documents for credit requests — an integrity check on the safety promise itself, not just its business effect; should be zero.
